title: Zaydi Alid dynasties
capsule: In the mid-ninth to early tenth century, the mountainous rim of the Caspian Sea—Tabaristan, Daylam, and Gilan—became the stronghold of a series of Zaydi Shi'a dynasties claiming descent from Ali ibn Abi Talib: the Alavids (864–928) and the Zaydis of Gilan. Hasan ibn Zayd founded the first emirate in Tabaristan in 864, capitalizing on local resistance to Abbasid tax collectors; his successors alternately ruled and were expelled by the Saffarids and Samanids. The dynasties served as conduits for Zaydi Islam into the Caspian region and kept the area outside orthodox Sunni control until Samanid consolidation around 928–930.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Territorial control fluctuated rapidly and is described only in Arabic literary sources (Tabari, Ibn Isfandiyar); precise geographic boundaries within the Caspian highlands are speculative.
